questions.q: What problem does a namespace prefix solve for a managed package?
options: It speeds up Apex compilation
It prevents the package's components from colliding with, or being confused with, something the customer already built in their own org
It automatically increments the package's version number
It encrypts all record data in the installing org
questions.explain: A namespace is a collision-prevention mechanism: it guarantees a managed package's components (fields, classes) are distinguishable from anything the installing customer's org already has, which matters especially since managed package code is hidden.

questions.q: What does Salesforce recommend regarding how many namespaces an organization should use across its managed 2GP packages?
options: A unique namespace for every single package
A single namespace shared across all of that organization's managed 2GP packages, since it makes cross-package code sharing easier
No namespace at all for managed packages
A new namespace for every package version
questions.explain: Salesforce explicitly recommends sharing one namespace across all of an organization's 2GP managed packages, since components across packages in the same namespace can reference each other more directly.

questions.q: Where is a namespace created, versus where is it registered/linked?
options: Created and registered both happen in the Dev Hub
Created in a dedicated Developer Edition org, then registered/linked to the Dev Hub through the Namespace Registry
Created in a scratch org, then registered in a sandbox
Both steps happen automatically with no org involved
questions.explain: A namespace is created in a dedicated Developer Edition org (reserving the prefix), then separately registered/linked to the Dev Hub via the Namespace Registry under Setup.

questions.q: What happens once a namespace has been associated with an org?
options: It can be freely changed or reused on another org at any time
It cannot be changed or reused elsewhere — the association is permanent
It automatically expires after the org's scratch org duration ends
It reverts to unregistered status after 30 days
questions.explain: Once a namespace is associated with an org, that association cannot be changed or reused elsewhere — which is why real production namespaces should never be linked carelessly to throwaway test orgs.

questions.q: After a namespace is registered, how does it get tied to actual package creation in a project?
options: Through the namespace property in sfdx-project.json, which any 2GP package created from that project becomes associated with
Through a separate namespace.json file unrelated to sfdx-project.json
Namespaces cannot be referenced from project configuration at all
Through the scratch org definition file's edition property
questions.explain: Once registered, a namespace is declared in the project's sfdx-project.json via the namespace property, and any new 2GP package created from that project becomes associated with the namespace named there.
